newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern offers talks with Conrail.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern offers talks with Conrail.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said it has offered to discuss East Coast rail competition with rivals Conrail Inc and CSX Corp, but again stressed it would only enter a pact that values Conrail at $115 per share.
Conrail has repeatedly rejected Norfolk Southern's acquisition offer in favor of a lower bid from CSX Corp.

In a letter to Conrail chairman David LeVan and CSX Corp chairman John Snow, Norfolk Southern chief David Goode wrote that he believes the three railroads can achieve balanced competition on the East Coast.

"The Conrail shareholders' vote last Friday places a responsibility on us to work out a rail structure in the East that will be in the long-term interests of all constituencies served by our companies. I believe that this can be accomplished if we sit down and try," Goode wrote.
Last week, LeVan also said he would be willing to talk about competitive issues with Norfolk Southern.
Conrail shareholders on Friday defeated a measure that was crucial to the proposed union of Conrail and CSX.
Conrail and CSX officials have vowed to bring the issue to another shareholder vote.
